Analyze languages in a Git revision, or profile a plain directory without Git. With no subcommand, emit the github-linguist directory output format. Git repository roots use committed HEAD content by default; --source directory scans current files.

Automation: --json emits data on stdout; diagnostics and warnings go to stderr. Success exits 0; handled errors exit 1. Successful reports may have partial coverage: inspect module status, coverage, and omissions. Empty language statistics do not prove an empty directory; analyze discovery inventories metadata. Legacy --json and analyze all --json have different output contracts. Use capabilities --cli --json for CLI contracts, capabilities --guide for workflows, and capabilities --schema profile --json for an offline schema. Plain capabilities describes planning modules; plan creates inert saved-report follow-ups.

Usage:
  dircue [path] [flags]
  dircue [command]

Examples:
  dircue --json /checkout
  dircue analyze discovery --source directory --json /content
  dircue analyze all --declarations --json /checkout
  dircue capabilities --cli --json

Available Commands:
  analyze      Run a selected profiler
  capabilities Describe modules supported by saved-report planning
  compare      Compare two saved profiles without rescanning their sources
  help         Help about any command
  plan         Plan selected follow-up analysis from a saved profile

Flags:
  -b, --breakdown            Include file paths in language results
  -h, --help                 help for dircue
  -j, --json                 Emit JSON
      --max-file-bytes int   Skip files larger than this many bytes (0 disables the optional size limit)
      --on-error string      Per-file read errors: fail or continue with explicit omissions (default "fail")
  -r, --rev string           Git revision to analyze (default "HEAD")
      --source string        Content source: auto (Git when present), git, or directory (default "auto")
  -s, --strategies           Show the language detection strategy for each file (text output)
      --tree string          Exact Git tree object ID to analyze (mutually exclusive with --rev)
  -t, --tree-size int        Maximum number of files scanned (default 100000)
  -v, --version              version for dircue
      --workers int          Number of concurrent file workers (0 selects automatically)

Use "dircue [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Choose the profiler for the evidence you need. Discovery inventories metadata; languages retains Linguist-compatible output; all combines languages and ecosystem hints with explicitly selected optional modules. Git repository roots use committed HEAD unless --source directory is selected. No heavier profiler is enabled by choosing this group.

Run the default language and filename-based detectors in one scan. Optional profilers run only when requested through flags such as --discovery, --declarations, --environments, --metrics, and --structure. Each module retains its own population, coverage, and omissions; totals need not describe identical files. Structural analysis requires an explicitly selected worker.

  dircue analyze projects [path] [flags]

Examples:
  dircue analyze projects --json /checkout
  dircue analyze all --projects --declarations --json /checkout

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for projects

Global Flags:
  -b, --breakdown            Include file paths in language results
  -j, --json                 Emit JSON
      --max-file-bytes int   Skip files larger than this many bytes (0 disables the optional size limit)
      --on-error string      Per-file read errors: fail or continue with explicit omissions (default "fail")
  -r, --rev string           Git revision to analyze (default "HEAD")
      --source string        Content source: auto (Git when present), git, or directory (default "auto")
  -s, --strategies           Show the language detection strategy for each file (text output)
      --tree string          Exact Git tree object ID to analyze (mutually exclusive with --rev)
  -t, --tree-size int        Maximum number of files scanned (default 100000)
      --workers int          Number of concurrent file workers (0 selects automatically)

Read bounded NuGet.Config and .npmrc files from the selected source. Report declarations and sanitized URL origins, never an effective feed set. No configuration discovery outside the selected source, variable expansion, network requests, or package-manager execution. Qualified identifiers and origins can reveal internal infrastructure names. Inspect scope, syntax status, and omissions before interpreting absence.

Apply a caller-supplied JSON ruleset to selected regular files, including files outside language statistics. Metadata predicates run before bounded complete-file literal matching. Rules add observations; they cannot disable modules, change language inclusion, execute commands, or load other configuration. Inspect coverage and omitted candidates before treating results as complete.

Run a trusted structural worker on bounded selected source files. Requires --structural-worker; the worker is executable code, not a sandbox. Unsupported languages, parse errors, file limits, and module scope remain visible. --functions adds function records; --hotspots ranks supported measurements without assigning a software-quality grade.

Usage:
  dircue analyze structure [path] [flags]

Examples:
  dircue analyze structure --structural-worker /tools/dircue-structural-worker --json /checkout
  dircue analyze structure --structural-worker /tools/dircue-structural-worker --functions --hotspots --json /checkout

Flags:
      --files                           Include per-file metrics or structural observations
      --functions                       Include bounded function-space metrics from the structural worker
  -h, --help                            help for structure
      --hotspots                        Summarize measured function populations and retain highest-valued metric evidence
      --structural-max-file-bytes int   Maximum complete source bytes for structural analysis (at most 8388608) (default 8388608)
      --structural-timeout duration     Time limit for each structural worker invocation (default 10s)
      --structural-worker string        Path to the optional native structural worker
